title: Air blower on paved entrances, landings and balconies
audience: Cleaners who use a handheld or backpack air blower to clear leaves and loose debris from paved entrances, landings, porches, balconies and stairwells.
learningOutcomes: Prepare an external area for blowing by clearing objects and surveying the area, neighbours and wind.
Blow debris in a controlled direction, away from cleaned areas, and collect it with a dustpan and banister brush.
Apply eye, hearing, respiratory and smoking controls for blower work.

instruction.heading: What blowing does and does not do
instruction.body: An air blower moves loose leaves and light debris quickly across open hard surfaces. It does not remove grease, stains or compacted soil, and those need the approved wet method. Blowing also lifts dust and fine debris into the air, so the work must control who is nearby and where the air is aimed.

instruction.heading: Set the direction before you start
instruction.body: Look over the site first, and set the nozzle or chute so air pushes the debris where you intend it to go. Open a lane along the centre line of the area first. Then work outward on alternating sides, so the debris is pushed away from cleaned sections and not back across them.

instruction.heading: Protect the operator and bystanders
instruction.body: Wear eye protection, hearing protection and any respiratory protection the task requires. Keep both hands on the blower while it runs. Debris can bounce back and strike the eyes, so keep people, pets and vehicles clear of the air stream. Do not smoke while you operate the blower or refuel it, and keep fuel and flames apart.

instruction.heading: Finish with a collection step
instruction.body: Blowing by itself leaves debris heaped against walls, door sills and fire doors. Sweep each heap into a dustpan with a banister brush; then place what you have collected in the general waste container. Do not blow debris into drains, gutters or neighbouring spaces.

procedure: Clear large objects from the area and survey the area, the neighbours and the wind direction.
Put on the PPE the task requires: eye protection, hearing protection and any respirator the site specifies.
Adjust the nozzle or chute so the debris moves away from your work area.
Start the blower as its instructions state, with both hands on the unit.
Open a lane along the centre line of the area first.
Push debris away from finished sections, switching sides as you go, until the surface is free of it.
Heap the remaining debris and collect it with a dustpan and banister brush.
Place the collected debris in the designated waste container.
Switch the blower off, clean and store it, take off the PPE and wash your hands.

workedExamples.situation: You are blowing leaves off a balcony, and a neighbour's washing is hanging close to the work area.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you keep blowing in the same direction?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Change the nozzle direction or move your position so the air does not blow debris onto the washing or into the neighbour's space. Pause if people come close, and resume only when the path is clear.

workedExamples.situation: A stairwell landing has leaves piled against the handrail and the base of a fire door, and the fire door must stay clear.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you handle the area by the fire door?
workedExamples.reasoning: Keep the route to the fire door free of debris and equipment. Push the foliage clear of the door, gather it with a dustpan so the exit stays open, and never leave the blower or waste on the landing.

equipmentAndPpe: Respiratory protection where the task or site rules require it
Dustpan, banister brush and waste container

commonErrors.error: Blowing debris back across areas that have already been cleaned.
commonErrors.prevention: Clear a path first, then work outward so the debris moves away from cleaned sections.
Put on eye and hearing protection before starting the blower.

commonErrors.error: Leaving debris piled against a fire exit.
commonErrors.prevention: Collect the debris and keep the exit path clear before you leave the area.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Fire exits and stairwells must stay clear of debris and equipment.
Blower use can expose the operator to noise, vibration and exhaust emissions.
This lesson does not grant any licence or authority to use a blower on property that is not the site being cleaned, or near services. Check the site's permission first.

qualityStandard: Debris is moved away from cleaned areas and collected.
Fire exits and stairwell paths are clear at handover.
Operator protection is worn throughout the task.
The blower is stored clean and serviceable.
documentationEvidence: Area record showing the blower task completed
Defect report if the blower is damaged or leaking fuel
summary: Clear and survey first, then blow in a controlled direction.
Protect eyes, ears and airways, and never smoke near the blower.
Collect the debris and keep fire exits clear.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must the blowing path be cleared first?
options: So the blower starts more easily when the path is left full of debris.
So the debris moves away from cleaned areas, not back across them.
So the fuel lasts longer and the blower uses less of it on the path.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should blown debris go before the area is handed over?
options: Left in piles against the wall to dry until the team leader can collect it later.
Gathered with a dustpan and banister brush and placed in the designated waste container.
Blown into the neighbour's yard when the wind is blowing that way at the time.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which protective approach is correct for blower work?
options: Eye and hearing protection, both hands on the blower, and no smoking nearby.
Sunglasses only, because the debris is light and the job is quick.
Hearing protection is optional on short tasks, and gloves are enough for the job.
